source: Directive tables of the Bareos 25.1.2 Director as carried by odir (crates/odir/src/commands/show_items.rs) plus Onesimus extensions (crates/odir/src/config_check.rs EXTENSIONS)
description: A FileSet resource says what a backup job saves: the Include blocks list files and plugins with Options blocks for compression, signatures and patterns; Exclude blocks leave things out.

examples.title: Linux system with excludes
examples.explanation: The first Options block whose patterns match decides: .cache directories and *.tmp files are excluded, everything else on ext4, xfs and btrfs file systems is saved with checksum and compression.

examples.title: A database through a plugin

directives.name: Name
directives.description: Name of the FileSet.

directives.name: Description
directives.description: Free text describing the FileSet.

examples.console: configure update fileset=LinuxAll description="All local file systems"

directives.name: Include
directives.description: Block with the files to back up (File, Plugin) and Options blocks that say how. A FileSet may have several Include blocks. See the Include block.

directives.name: Exclude
directives.description: Block with files and directories to leave out (File lines). Patterns go into an Options block with Exclude = yes instead.

directives.name: Ignore File Set Changes
directives.description: Normally a change of the FileSet makes the next Incremental or Differential a Full, since the old backups do not contain the new files. With yes the change is ignored; new files then only appear in the next Full.

directives.name: Enable VSS
directives.description: On Windows clients: back up from a Volume Shadow Copy snapshot, so open files are consistent.

blocks.name: Include
blocks.description: Files and plugins to back up, with Options blocks.

directives.name: File
directives.description: A file or directory to back up; directories are backed up recursively. Repeat it for several paths. "|command" uses the output of a command on the Director as list, "\\|command" one run on the client, and "<file" ("\\<file" on the client) reads the list from a file.

directives.name: Plugin
directives.description: A File Daemon plugin with its options that delivers the data instead of files, for example a database plugin. The Onesimus Director masks secrets in plugin lines in show output and in the FileSet text stored in the catalog; the File Daemon still gets the real line.

directives.name: Exclude Dir Containing
directives.description: Leave out every directory that contains a file of this name, so users can mark directories with a .nobackup file.

directives.name: Options
directives.description: Block of options for the files of this Include. Several Options blocks may be given: the first block whose patterns match a file decides; a block without patterns applies to all remaining files. See the Options block.

blocks.name: Exclude
blocks.description: Files and directories to leave out.

directives.name: File
directives.description: A file or directory that is left out. Wildcards are not interpreted here; use an Options block with Wild and Exclude = yes for patterns.

blocks.name: Options
blocks.description: Options of an Include block. Several blocks may be given; the first block whose patterns (Wild, Regex, ...) match a file decides, a block without patterns applies to all other files. The option keywords and values follow the Onesimus Director's port of the C++ table (inc_conf.cc); Hard Links defaults to no, Acl Support and Xattr Support to yes.

directives.name: Signature
directives.description: Checksum stored for every file, used by verify jobs and Accurate mode to detect changes. XXH128 is fast; SHA256 or SHA512 are cryptographic. Without it no checksum is stored.

directives.name: Compression
directives.description: Software compression on the client. LZ4 is fast with moderate gain, GZIP6 (= GZIP) compresses better but costs CPU. Leave it off for data that is compressed already and for tape drives that compress in hardware (see Allow Compression of the Storage).

directives.name: Encryption
directives.description: Cipher for data encryption on the client. Encryption also needs PKI keys in the File Daemon's configuration; without the private key the data cannot be restored.

directives.name: Force Encryption
directives.description: Fail the job instead of backing up unencrypted when encryption is not possible.

directives.name: One FS
directives.description: Stay on the file system of each File line and do not descend into other mounted file systems. With no, mount points are crossed; then FS Type helps to skip /proc, /sys and network file systems.

directives.name: Recurse
directives.description: Back up directories recursively. With no, only the entries directly in a listed directory are saved.

directives.name: Sparse
directives.description: Store sparse files efficiently (holes are not stored), for example virtual machine images.

directives.name: Hard Links
directives.description: Detect hard links and store the data of a multiply linked file once. In Bareos 25 the default is no (each link is saved as a file), which saves memory on clients with many files; the Onesimus Director has the same default.

directives.name: Replace
directives.description: Default replace mode for restores of these files.

directives.name: Read Fifo
directives.description: Read the data from named pipes (FIFOs) instead of saving them as special files, for example to back up a database dump written into a pipe by a Client Run Before Job script.

directives.name: Portable
directives.description: On Windows: store files in a portable format (without Windows backup streams), so they can be restored on other systems, at the cost of security information.

directives.name: Mtime Only
directives.description: Select files for Incremental and Differential backups by modification time only, ignoring the change time (ctime).

directives.name: Keep Atime
directives.description: Reset the access time of each file after reading it. This changes the ctime, so Incrementals would save the files again unless Mtime Only is set; Noatime is usually the better choice.

directives.name: Noatime
directives.description: Open files with O_NOATIME so reading does not change the access time (Linux, file owner or root).

directives.name: Exclude
directives.description: The files matched by the patterns of this Options block are excluded instead of included.

directives.name: Acl Support
directives.description: Back up POSIX and NFSv4 ACLs. Default yes in Bareos 25 and in the Onesimus Director.

directives.name: Xattr Support
directives.description: Back up extended attributes (for example SELinux labels). Default yes in Bareos 25.

directives.name: Ignore Case
directives.description: Match Wild and Regex patterns without regard to case; useful for Windows clients.

directives.name: Hfs Plus Support
directives.description: On macOS: back up HFS+ resource forks and Finder information.

directives.name: Enhanced Wild
directives.description: Accepted for compatibility; the Director stores it like Noatime (the C++ Director does the same).

directives.name: Check File Changes
directives.description: Check after reading a file whether it changed while it was saved, and warn if so.

directives.name: Honor No Dump Flag
directives.description: Skip files that carry the nodump flag (chattr +d).

directives.name: Shadowing
directives.description: Detects File lines that lie inside other File lines (and would be saved twice): warn about them or remove them, within this Include (local) or the whole FileSet (global).

directives.name: Auto Exclude
directives.description: On Windows: honour the files the system lists as not to be backed up (FilesNotToBackup).

directives.name: Verify
directives.description: Attributes compared by verify jobs, as option letters: i inode, p permissions, n links, u user, g group, s size, a atime, m mtime, c ctime, d size decrease, 5 MD5, 1 SHA1.

directives.name: Accurate
directives.description: Attributes compared in Accurate mode to decide whether a file changed, as option letters like Verify (default mcs: mtime, ctime and size).

directives.name: Strip Path
directives.description: Removes this many leading path components before the files are stored.

directives.name: Size
directives.description: Select files by size: a size, a range (10k-1m) or a comparison (<1m, >1g).

directives.name: Wild
directives.description: Shell wildcard (* ? [ ]) matched against the full path; repeatable. Files that match are handled by this Options block (included, or excluded with Exclude = yes).

directives.name: Wild Dir
directives.description: Wildcard matched against directory paths only.

directives.name: Wild File
directives.description: Wildcard matched against file names (not directories); a pattern without / matches the base name.

directives.name: Regex
directives.description: POSIX extended regular expression matched against the full path; repeatable.

directives.name: Regex Dir
directives.description: Regular expression matched against directory paths only.

directives.name: Regex File
directives.description: Regular expression matched against file paths only.

directives.name: FS Type
directives.description: Only back up file systems of these types (ext4, xfs, btrfs, ...). Together with One FS = no it selects the local file systems and skips proc, sysfs, tmpfs and network mounts.

directives.name: Drive Type
directives.description: On Windows: only back up drives of these types (fixed, removable, remote, cdrom, ramdisk).

directives.name: Meta
directives.description: Meta information passed to plugins.

directives.name: Plugin
directives.description: Plugin that handles the files of this Options block.
